akhfash:5-5.t:
He said ﴿سَلاَمٌ هِيَ﴾, that is: it is peace (هِي سلامٌ); He means: kept safe (مُسَلَّمَة).
And He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ﴾: He means the rising (الطلوع). The maṣdar (verbal noun) here is built only on "مَفْعَل".

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ﴾, that is, the Qur'an, all at once, from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven ﴿فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ﴾, that is, of honour and greatness.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ﴾: made you know, O Muhammad, ﴿مَا لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ﴾: a magnifying of its matter and an expression of wonder at it.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ﴾ that do not contain the Night of Qadr; so righteous work in it is better than in a thousand months that do not contain it.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ — with one of the two tāʾs of the original dropped — ﴿وَالرُّوحُ﴾, that is, Jibrīl, ﴿فِيهَا﴾: in the night ﴿بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: by His command ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ﴾ that Allah has decreed in it for that year until the next. «من» is causal (sababiyya), in the sense of «الباء».

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿سَلَامٌ هِيَ﴾: a fronted khabar (predicate) and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿حَتَّى مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ﴾ — with fatḥa and with kasra on the lām — until the time of its rising. It was made "peace" because of the abundance of greetings of peace in it from the angels; they do not pass by a believing man or woman without greeting them with peace.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿أَنْزَلْناهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position; ﴿فِي لَيْلَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْقَدْرِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a resumptive particle; ﴿وَما﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿ما لَيْلَةُ﴾: mubtadaʾ and its khabar; ﴿الْقَدْرِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the nominal clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), muḍāf to القدر; ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position; ﴿مِنْ أَلْفِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خير; ﴿شَهْرٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلائِكَةُ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive; ﴿وَالرُّوحُ﴾: conjoined to الملائكة; ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿بِإِذْنِ﴾: also attached to the verb; ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿أَمْرٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿سَلامٌ هِيَ﴾: fronted khabar (predicate) and postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive; ﴿حَتَّى مَطْلَعِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) سلام; ﴿الْفَجْرِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

dervis-irab:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ وَما أَدْراكَ ما لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ) (إن) and its noun, and the clause (أنزلناه) is its predicate, meaning: in scattered portions, according to events and the pressing need for it, over the span of twenty-three years. In the pronoun's referring to the Qur'an (أنزلناه) although it has not been mentioned before, there is a testimony to its honour; and He ascribed it to Himself, the Exalted, and made it exclusively His own to the exclusion of anyone else; and He raised the standing of the period of time in which it was sent down. These are three ways of magnifying the Qur'an. (في ليلة القدر) are two elements attached to (أنزلناه) — the discussion of it will come in the section on Benefits. (الواو) is a conjunction. (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause (أدراك) is its khabar (predicate). (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (ليلة القدر) is the khabar of (ما). The clause suspended by the interrogative stands in the place of the second object of (أدراك). (لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ)
(ليلة القدر) is a mubtadaʾ and (خير) is the khabar; (من ألف شهر) are two elements attached to (خير); and the clause is resumptive, as if it were the answer to a question arising from the magnification of the Night of Power, the question being, in its implied form: "And what are its merits?" (تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيها بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ) A second resumptive clause, introduced as an answer to the same question. (تنزل) is an imperfect verb in the nominative; its original form is (تتنزل). (الملائكة) is the fāʿil (agent), and (الروح) is conjoined to (الملائكة). Gabriel was singled out for mention only to extol his excellence, along the lines of His saying, the Exalted, (فِيهِمَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَنَخْلٌ وَرُمَّانٌ), since the date palm and the pomegranate are among the fruits. (فيها) are two elements attached to (تنزل); you may also attach it to an omitted element serving as ḥāl (circumstantial) from (الملائكة), meaning "accompanied by". (بإذن ربهم) are two elements attached to (تنزل). (من كل أمر), meaning "for the sake of every matter that Allah decreed for that year", is attached to (تنزل). (سَلامٌ هِيَ حَتَّى مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ) (سلام) is a preposed khabar and (هي) is a postposed mubtadaʾ. (حتى) is a particle of limit and genitive case, and (مطلع الفجر) is genitive after (حتى); the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (سلام). There is a difficulty in this, namely the separation between the maṣdar (verbal noun) and its dependent by the mubtadaʾ. The answer is that adverbs and prepositional phrases are given a latitude that others are not given. The better view, as al-Khaṭīb said, is that the two are attached to an omitted element, which al-Khaṭīb put as: "they continue in greeting from sunset until the rising of dawn."

* Benefits:
Al-Qurṭubī said: The Night of Power is peace and goodness throughout, with no evil in it until the rising of dawn. Allah willed to conceal it so that whoever seeks it would spend many nights alive in worship, so that his devotion would increase and his reward be multiplied, and so that people, were it made known, would not rely on having obtained its merit and then neglect other nights. On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Power out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins are forgiven; and whoever fasts Ramadan out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins are forgiven." Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. His words "out of faith and seeking reward" (īmānan wa-ḥtisāban) mean: with intention and resolve; that is, that one fasts it in belief and in desire for its reward, willingly, not disliking it, nor finding its fasting burdensome, nor finding its days long, but regarding the length of its days as a gain because of the greatness of the reward. Iḥtisāb derives from ḥasb, as iʿtidād derives from ʿadd (counting). It is said of one who intends the face of Allah by his deed, "iḥtasabahu", because he then has the right to count (yaʿtadd) his deed, so that during the performance of the act it is as though he is counting it. Al-Baghawī said: His word "iḥtisāban" means: seeking the face of Allah, the Exalted, and His reward. It is said, "So-and-so iḥtasibu the reports and taḥassabuhā", that is, he seeks them out. That being so, whoever wishes to go further should consult the longer works, for in them are so many reports about this night and its merits that the pages and volumes cannot contain them.

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَآ أَدْرَاكَ مَا لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ﴾.
Everything in the Qurʾān in the form of His words "وما أدراك" (and what has made you know?), He has made him know it; and whatever is in the form of His words "وما يدريك" (and what makes you know?), He has not made him know it.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيْلَةُ ٱلْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِّنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ﴾.
[144/b] He says: deeds on the Night of Decree are better than deeds in a thousand months in which there is no Night of Decree. And the Night of Decree — according to what Ḥibbān mentioned from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās — is in every month of Ramaḍān.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَنَزَّلُ ٱلْمَلاَئِكَةُ وَٱلرُّوحُ فِيهَا﴾.
It is said that Gabriel ﷺ descends and with him the angels, and they do not meet a believing man or a believing woman without greeting him with peace. [Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us;] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh narrated to me from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he used to read: ﴿مِنْ كِلِّ امرىءٍ(4) سَلاَمٌ﴾ (5) [i.e. "from every man: peace"]. This agrees with the tafsīr of al-Kalbī, and no one other than Ibn ʿAbbās read it so.
The reading of the generality [of readers] stops at His word ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ﴾ and then begins anew, saying: ﴿سَلاَمٌ هِيَ حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ﴾. As for (المطلِع), Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb alone read it with kasra, while the generality read it with fatḥa on the lām (مطلَع).
The reading of the generality is stronger by the analogy (qiyās) of Arabic, because «المطلَع» with fatḥa is the rising [itself], while «المطلِع» is the place of sunrise, the spot from which it rises — except that the Arabs say: طلعت الشمسُ مطلِعا (the sun rose a rising), with kasra, meaning the maṣdar (verbal noun), just as you say: أكرمتك كرامةً (I honoured you with honour), making do with the noun in place of the maṣdar. Likewise your saying: أعطيتك عطاء (I gave you a gift): the noun is made to suffice in place of the maṣdar.

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «وما أدراك» is resumptive; the clause «أدراك» is the khabar (predicate) of «ما»; and the clause «ما ليلة» is the second object of «أدراك».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: (ليلة القدر خير من ألف شهر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; the preposition «من ألف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خير».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «تَنزل» is resumptive; the preposition «بإذن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «تَنزل»; the preposition «من كل» is attached to «تَنزل».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «سلام»: a fronted khabar (predicate); «هي»: a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later; «حتى»: a particle of limit and genitive; «مطلع»: a genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) {تَنَزَّلُ}; and the clause (هي سلام) is parenthetical between the preposition and what it is attached to.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر): the hāʾ refers back to the Qur'an, although there has been no mention of it, since the meaning is understood.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما ليلة القدر): the first (ما) is an interrogative, a mubtadaʾ (subject); (أدراك) is a verb containing the agent pronoun referring back to (ما), and the kāf is the first object of (أدراك). The second (ما) is an interrogative, a second mubtadaʾ, and (ليلة) is the khabar (predicate) of the second; the clause is in the position of the second object of (أدراك). (أدراك) with its two objects is the khabar of the first (ما). Its like is (وما أدراك ما القارعة). The discussion of this has already preceded in al-Ḥāqqa and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His saying (سلام هي): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
His saying (حتى مطلع الفجر): the base in the analogy of (مطلع) is fatḥa on the lām, because the noun of place and the maṣdar (verbal noun) of faʿala yafʿulu are on the pattern mafʿal. Some words are irregular and came with kasra as a dialect, such as (المسجد) and (المجلس). Al-Kisāʾī read (مطلع) with kasra on the lām, making it among those that depart from their analogy.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إنا﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle, and ﴿نا﴾ is its noun (ism).
﴿أنزلناه﴾: a past verb, ﴿نا﴾ is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أنزلناه﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «إن».
﴿في ليلة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزلناه﴾.
﴿القدر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb, the agent is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate).
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿ليلة﴾: khabar of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿القدر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿ما ليلة القدر﴾ is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of the verb ﴿أدراك﴾. The clause ﴿وما أدراك...﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿ليلة القدر﴾ in the previous ayah.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿ليلة﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿القدر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿خير﴾: khabar (predicate).
﴿من ألف﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿خير﴾.
﴿شهر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿ليلة القدر خير﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿تنزل﴾: a second resumption; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, and «تنزل» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿الملائكة﴾: fāʿil (agent).
﴿والروح﴾: conjoined by a conjunction (ʿaṭf nasaq) to ﴿الملائكة﴾.
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تنزل﴾, or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الملائكة», i.e. "accompanied" (متلبسين).
﴿بإذن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تنزل﴾.
﴿ربهم﴾: «رب» is muḍāf, the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿من كل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تنزل﴾.
﴿أمر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿سلام﴾: a fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿هي﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿حتى﴾: a particle of limit and genitive.
﴿مطلع﴾: genitive (majrūr) by ﴿حتى﴾; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿سلام﴾.
﴿الفجر﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
إِنَّا: its original is إنّنا, and the nūn was dropped because of the gathering of nūns and because it is augmentative. أَنْزَلْناهُ: the nūn and the alif are in the position of the nominative as the agent of the verb, and the lām was made quiescent because of its attachment to the nominative pronoun, in conformity with (forms) in which vowels follow in succession. The hāʾ is in the position of the accusative, and the wāw after it was dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the alif, the hāʾ not being a strong barrier because of its faintness and remoteness (of articulation). It has also been said: because two letters of prolongation and softness came together, so one of them was dropped.
The hāʾ is a pronoun (kināya) for the Qur'an, even though it has not been mentioned before in this sūra. Most grammarians say: (this is) because the meaning is known, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 580- ألا ليتني أفديك منها وأفتدي ("Would that I could ransom you from it and be ransomed"). Among the scholars are those who say: the pronoun was permissible at the beginning of the sūra because the whole Qur'an is in the rank of a single sūra, since it was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven — and we shall mention this with its chain. A third view, clear and good, is that إنّا أنزلناه indicates the sending down and the thing sent down, as the grammarians report: من كذب كان شرّا له ("whoever lies, it is worse for him"), because كذب indicates lying.
The Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr) was hidden from people, except for what came in the ḥadīth that it is in the last ten (nights) of the month of Ramaḍān. It has been said: it was hidden only because of the merit of deeds in it, so that people would not abandon deeds and striving in other (nights) and rely on the merit of deeds in it. And it has been said: because it varies, being on the twenty-third in one year and then on another (night) in other years.
As for the ḥadīth about the sending down of the Qur'an all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, it is sound and not rejected among the people of the Sunna; only a party of the people of caprice (ahl al-ahwāʾ) rejects it. As was read before Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, who said: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ (1): he said: The Qur'an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven, and it was at the position of the stars, and Allah would send it down upon His Messenger, part of it after another; so they said: لَوْلا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً كَذلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ وَرَتَّلْناهُ تَرْتِيلًا [al-Furqān: 32].
As for naming it the Night of al-Qadr, there are two views on it. One of them is that it is the night of majesty and veneration, from their saying "so-and-so has standing (qadr)". The other view, which the early scholars held, is that it was named the Night of al-Qadr because the life-spans and provisions of the servants are decreed (tuqaddaru) in it, as Qatāda said: there is decreed in the Night of Decree what will be until the following year, of life-spans and provisions.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: ما is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and أَدْراكَ is a past verb in the position of the khabar (predicate); the kāf is in the position of the accusative. ما لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ is a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, and it carries the sense of magnification.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
A mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), i.e., deeds in it are better than deeds in a thousand months in which there is no Night of Decree.
This is the clear (meaning), even though it has been narrated from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: it is the thousand months in which the Banū Umayya ruled. He said: the Prophet ﷺ had been shown them on the pulpits, and that alarmed him; then their rule was counted afterwards and it was so. This is a narrated report; there is nothing in the apparent wording of the recitation that indicates it, and Allah knows best.

nahhas-irab:4-5.t:
تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيها بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ: the original is تتنزّل, and the tāʾ was dropped because two tāʾs came together. The exegetes said: بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ means by the command of their Lord. مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ: this is the end of the statement according to the grammarians, among them al-Farrāʾ. The meaning on their view is: the angels and the Spirit descend in it by the command of their Lord, i.e., they descend with the command of Allah in which are the life-spans and provisions, to the lowest heaven, from every matter, i.e., from every matter in which there is provision, life-span, pilgrimage for whoever performs pilgrimage, and so on.
Abū ʿUbayd reported that it was narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿIkrima that they read «من كلّ امرئ» ("from every person"). Ismāʿīl ibn Isḥāq said: Abū ʿUbayd did not mention its chain, and perhaps it is weak. Abū Jaʿfar said: Its chain is weak without any "perhaps": al-Kalbī narrated it from Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās, and this is a chain not to be relied upon; and it contradicts the codex (muṣḥaf) by which the proof is established. Whoever brings it thus says the complete statement is: من كل امرئ سلام, as al-Shaʿbī said: from every one of the angels, peace upon the believing men and believing women. And it has been said: the meaning is "from every fearsome matter, peace", i.e., safety.
On the reading of the community, سَلامٌ is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of هي, as you say قائم زيد ("standing is Zayd"), i.e., it is peace, i.e., an abode of safety, i.e., possessing safety. As was read before Muḥammad ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, who said: Jarīr narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhāl ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā: «سلام هي», he said: the devils do not act in it, sorcery is not possible in it, and nothing happens in it until dawn. Yūsuf said: and Tamīm ibn Ziyād narrated to us, saying: Abū Jaʿfar al-Rāzī narrated to us, from al-Rabīʿ, from Abū al-ʿĀliya: «سلام هي», he said: it is all good until the rising of the dawn. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: the rebellious devils are chained in it, and repentance is accepted in it. These are the views of the early exegetes. One [Translator's note: the text reads «بعد», apparently for «بعض», "some"] of the later ones said: the meaning of «سلام هي» is that only good is decreed in it, of provisions and pilgrimage, while evil is decreed in other (nights) — holding that concerning the night of mid-Shaʿbān a ḥadīth has come about the decreeing of things. These are the views of the early and the later ones, and Allah knows best what He intended.
حَتَّى مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ with fatḥa on the lām is the reading of the generality. Al-Farrāʾ said: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb alone read حَتَّى مَطْلِعِ الْفَجْرِ (with kasra). Abū Jaʿfar said: It is the reading of Abū Rajāʾ al-ʿUṭāridī. The best of what has been said about this is the saying of Sībawayh, who said: they used kasra in the maṣdar; they said أتيتك عند مطلِع الشمس, i.e., at the rising of the sun. This is the dialect of Banū Tamīm; as for the people of the Ḥijāz, they say مطلَع, and المطلِع is the place.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The explanation of this is that for whatever is on the pattern faʿala yafʿulu, the rule is that its maṣdar and its noun of place are mafʿal with fatḥa. Its noun of place ought to be with ḍamma, except that there is no mafʿul in the speech of the Arabs, so it had to be shifted to fatḥa or kasra, and the fatḥa was more fitting because it is lighter. The evidence for what we said is that whatever is on the pattern faʿala yafʿilu, its maṣdar is mafʿal with fatḥa, and the noun of place and time with kasra: they said jalasa majlasan ("he sat a sitting") and "he is in your majlis (sitting-place)", and for time: "the she-camel reached her maḍrib (time of mating)", with kasra. This shows you that the original is maṭlaʿ for the place, then it was shifted to fatḥa. Then things were heard from the Arabs which are taken by hearing, without analogy: they said maṭliʿ for the place where the sun rises, and some of them said maṭliʿ for the maṣdar. The fatḥa is more fitting, because the fatḥa in the maṣdar occurs for faʿala yafʿilu, so how (much more) would it be for faʿala yafʿulu? Moreover, the reading of the community, by whom the proof is established, is «حتّى مطلَع». This shows its strength in Arabic, and the anomalousness of the kasra and its departure from analogy.
Abū Ḥātim said: In the version (ḥarf) of Ubayy: «سلام هي إلى مطلع الفجر». Abū Jaʿfar said:
This reading is by way of explanation (tafsīr), and no one may recite with it, because it contradicts the great mass (al-sawād al-aʿẓam).

safi-cedvel:1-5.t:
* I'rab:
The pronoun in (أنزلناه) refers to the noble Qur'an, even though it has not been mentioned before, taking it from the attribution of its revelation to Him, the Exalted (في ليلة) is attached to (أنزلناه) ..
Clause: «إنّا أنزلناه ... » has no grammatical position; it is an opening clause.
And the clause: «أنزلناه ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of inna.
Verses 2-5: (الواو) is parenthetical (ما) is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative, a mubtadaʾ, in both places..
The khabar of the first is the clause أدراك, and the khabar of the second is (ليلة) [Note: it is possible that the second (ما) is a fronted khabar and (ليلة) a postponed mubtadaʾ.], the second (ليلة) is a nominative mubtadaʾ whose khabar is (خير) (من ألف) is attached to (خير), (تنزّل) is a nominative imperfect from which one of the two tāʾs was omitted (فيها) is attached to (تنزّل), (بإذن) is attached to (تنزّل) [Note: or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تنزّل, i.e. "being clothed (with permission)".], (من كلّ) is attached to (تنزّل) [Note: i.e. for the sake of every matter.. or attached to a ḥāl from the agent of تنزّل, i.e. "prepared for the sake of every matter".] and (من) denotes causation (سلام) is a fronted nominative khabar for the postponed mubtadaʾ (هي) [Note: it may be the pronoun of the night, and it may be the pronoun of the angels, and the verse is interpreted according to each.], (حتّى مطلع) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (سلام) [Note: or attached to (تنزّل).].
And the clause: «ما أدراك ... » has no grammatical position; it is parenthetical.
And the clause: «أدراك ... » is in the position of nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (ما).
And the clause: «ما ليلة ... » is in the position of accusative, a second mafʿūl bihi of the verb أدراك.
And the clause: «ليلة القدر خير ... » has no grammatical position; it is an explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «تنزّل الملائكة ... » has no grammatical position; it is another explanatory resumption.
And the clause: «سلام هي ... » has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(1) القدر: a proper noun for a particular night among the last ten of Ramadan; originally it is a maṣdar meaning "determination", or "honour", or "decree"; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.. And see verse (91) of Sūrat al-Anʿām.
(5) مطلع: a mīmī maṣdar from the triliteral طلع; its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
- The merit of the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr):
On the authority of Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever stands in prayer on the Night of Power out of faith and seeking reward, his past sins will be forgiven."
It occurs in every Ramadan until the Day of Resurrection, as the scholars unanimously agreed. It is said that it is in the last ten days, especially the odd nights among them. Some scholars said that it occurs on a fixed night that it does not exceed, and others said: it moves, so each year it falls at a place different from the previous year.
On the authority of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I know the Night of Power, what do I say in it?" He said: "Say: O Allah, You are Pardoning and Generous, You love pardon, so pardon me." Al-Tirmidhī transmitted it
and said: a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith. Its sign is that the sun rises on the morning of its day white, without rays, because the angels fill the expanse with their wings that night, so they do not allow the light of the sun to shine as usual.
It is a night in which worship outweighs the worship of a thousand months.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: A man of the Children of Israel was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who carried arms on his shoulder in the path of Allah for a thousand months, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ marvelled at that and wished the same for his community, and said: "O Lord, You have made my community the shortest of nations in lifespan and the fewest in deeds." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, gave him the Night of Power, and the Exalted said: (لَيْلَةُ الْقَدْرِ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أَلْفِ شَهْرٍ).
Al-Baghawī said: In sum, Allah the Exalted made this night obscure to the community so that they would strive in worship during the nights of the month of Ramadan, hoping to attain it, just as He concealed the hour of answer on Friday, concealed the middle prayer among the five prayers, His greatest name in the Qur'an among His names, His pleasure in acts of obedience, that they may be eager for all of them, and His anger in acts of disobedience, that they may desist from all of them.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ}, i.e. the Qurʾān; it was implied [as a pronoun] because it is known. «في ليلةِ القَدْر» may be an adverbial of time for the sending down. In the exegesis: He sent it down to the lowest heaven on this night, then it came down to the earth in instalments over twenty years. It was also said: the meaning is: He sent down [revelation] concerning its standing and merit; so it is not an adverbial, but rather it is like the saying of ʿUmar: «خَشِيْتُ أَنْ يَنْزِلَ فيَّ قرآنٌ» (I feared that Qurʾān would be sent down concerning me), and the saying of ʿĀʾisha: «لأَنا أَحْقَرُ في نفسي أَنْ يَنْزِل فيَّ قرآنٌ» (I am too insignificant in my own eyes for Qurʾān to be sent down concerning me). It was called ليلة القَدْر either because of the decreeing (taqdīr) of affairs in it, or because of its being narrow (ḍīq) with the angels.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {والروح فِيهَا}: «الرُّوحُ» may be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), the preposition with its noun after it being the khabar (predicate); or it may be nominative as fāʿil (agent), conjoined onto «الملائكة», with «فيها» attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَنَزَّلُ».
His saying: {بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم}: It may be attached to «تَنَزَّلُ», or attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of what is made nominative by «تَنَزَّلُ», i.e. accompanied by the permission of their Lord.
His saying: {مِّن كُلِّ أَمْرٍ}: Two views are possible on «مِنْ». The first: it is in the sense of the lām and is attached to «تَنَزَّلُ», i.e. they descend for the sake of every matter decreed until the following year. The second: it is in the sense of the bāʾ, i.e. they descend with every matter, so it is for transitivity (taʿdiya); Abū Ḥātim said this. The majority read «أَمْرٍ», the singular of الأمور (matters). Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿIkrima and al-Kalbī [read] «امْرِئٍ», the masculine of امرأة, i.e. for the sake of every human being; it was also said: for the sake of every angel, and that is far-fetched. It was also said: «مِنْ كلِّ أَمْرٍ» is not attached to «تَنَزَّلُ»; it is attached only to what comes after it, i.e. it is peace from every fearful matter. Taken literally this does not hold, because «سَلامٌ» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and its governed word does not precede it; what is meant is only that it is attached to an omitted [word] indicated by this maṣdar.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {سَلاَمٌ هِيَ}: There are two views on it. The first: «هي» is the pronoun of the angels, and «سلام» means greeting, i.e. the angels are [bearers] of greeting to the believers; in the exegesis: they greet every believing man and woman on that night with a salutation. The second: it is the pronoun of the Night of Decree, and «سلام» means safety, i.e. the Night of Decree is [a night] of safety from anything feared. On either supposition, «سلامٌ» may be nominative as a fronted khabar (predicate) with «هي» a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), and this is the well-known [view]; or it may be nominative as mubtadaʾ with «هي» as its fāʿil (agent) according to al-Akhfash, because he does not stipulate [the adjective's] reliance [on a preceding word] for it to govern. It has already been stated that some make the speech complete at His saying {بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِم} and attach «مِنْ كلِّ أمرٍ» to what follows it, and its interpretation has been given.
Abū al-Faḍl [al-Rāzī] said: «It was said: its meaning is: it is peace from every matter, or [every] person (امرئ), i.e. safe or kept safe from it. It is not permissible that "سلامٌ" — this overt word, which is the maṣdar — govern what precedes it, because the governed word of the maṣdar may not precede the maṣdar, just as the ṣila (relative clause) is likewise not permitted to precede the relative noun.» End of quotation. It has been stated that the meaning of that, according to the one who holds it, is that it is attached to an omitted [word] indicated by «سَلام»; so it is an explanation of meaning, not an explanation of i'rab. As for what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās — that the speech is complete at His saying, the Exalted, {سلامٌ}, and one begins with «هي» as the khabar of a mubtadaʾ [sic], the reference by «ذلك» being to its being the twenty-seventh night, because the word «هي» is the twenty-seventh of the words of this sūra, as if it were said: the Night of Decree is the one corresponding in number to the word «هي» among the words of this sūra — its authenticity should not be believed, because it is riddling and a mutilation of the composition of eloquent speech. [Translator's note: «على أنَّها خبرُ مبتدأ» is as written; on this reading «هي» would rather be a mubtadaʾ. The «ذلك» referred to is not otherwise specified in the passage.]
His saying: {هِيَ حتى مَطْلَعِ}: [«حتى مطلع»] is attached to «تَنَزَّلُ» or to «سَلامٌ»; and there is a difficulty in [the latter] because of the separation between the maṣdar and its governed word by the mubtadaʾ, unless latitude is allowed for the preposition [with its noun]. [Translator's note: the text reads «إلاَّ يُتَوَسَّعَ», evidently for «إلاَّ أَنْ يُتَوَسَّعَ»; translated accordingly.] In the exegesis: they continue greeting the believing people until dawn rises. Al-Kisāʾī read «مَطْلِعِ» with kasra on the lām, and the rest with fatḥa. The fatḥa is according to analogy (qiyās) and the kasra is by hearing (samāʿ); it has sister forms in which the kasra is preserved among those whose imperfect has ḍamma or fatḥa [on the middle radical], such as المَشْرِق and المَجْزِر. Are both [forms] verbal nouns, or is the fatḥa form a verbal noun and the kasra form a noun of place? There is disagreement. On every supposition, the analogy for مَفْعِل in general, among verbs whose imperfect has ḍamma or fatḥa on the middle radical, is fatḥa on the middle radical; the distinction occurs only in sound verbs with kasra on the middle radical, such as يَضْرِب.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ (١)).
The hāʾ in (أَنْزَلْنَاهُ) refers to the Mighty Qurʾān, although it has not been mentioned here.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالرُّوحُ فِيهَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ أَمْرٍ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (وَالرُّوحُ): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with «فِيهَا» as the khabar (predicate), or it may be maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the fāʿil (agent). «فِيهَا» is an adverbial (ẓarf) or a ḥāl (circumstantial). The words of the Exalted (بِإِذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ): the bāʾ may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَتَنَزَّلُ», or it may be a ḥāl. [Translator's note: the author writes «تَتَنَزَّلُ», the unabbreviated form of the verb read in the muṣḥaf as «تَنَزَّلُ».]

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (سَلَامٌ هِيَ حَتَّى مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ (٥)).
The words of the Exalted (سَلَامٌ هِيَ): there are two views on «سَلَامٌ»:
The first: it is in the sense of «مُسَلِّمَة» (greeting with peace), i.e. the angels greet the believers with peace, or they greet one another. The second: it is in the sense of «سَلَامَة» (safety) or «تَسْلِيم» (greeting). On the first view, «هِيَ» is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and «سَلَامٌ» is a fronted khabar (predicate). «حَتَّى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «سَلَام», i.e. the angels are greeting with peace until the rising of the dawn.
It is also possible for «هِيَ» to be put in the nominative by «سَلَام», according to the view of al-Akhfash. On the second view, [the meaning is that] the Night of Decree is possessed of greeting, i.e. possessed of safety, until the rising of the dawn, and the two previous construals apply to it. It is also possible for «حَتَّى» to be attached to «تَنَزَّلُ». [Translator's note: the printed text reads «يَتَعَلَّقَ حَتَّى يَنْزِلَ»; it is translated here as referring to the verb «تَنَزَّلُ» of the previous verse.]
(مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ): with a kasra and with a fatḥa on the lām are two dialectal forms. It is said that the fatḥa is more in accordance with analogy (aqyas).

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Qadr
Medinan; and it was said: the correct view is that it is Meccan.
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ في لَيْلَةِ القَدْرِ﴾ ("We sent it down on the Night of Decree"): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the Qur'an. It has not been mentioned at the beginning of the sūra, but its mention occurred in what came before it [Translator's note: i.e. elsewhere in the Qur'an], namely His saying: ﴿حم﴾ [al-Dukhān: 1] ﴿والكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 2] ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْناهُ في لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 3] ("Ḥā Mīm. By the clear Book. We sent it down on a blessed night"), and that is the Night of Decree. The meaning of ”لَيْلَةُ القَدْرِ“ is "the night of ruling (ḥukm)"; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿فِيها يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾ [al-Dukhān: 4] ("in it every wise matter is made distinct"). The whole Qur'an was sent down to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree; then Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought it down to the Prophet ﷺ over twenty years.

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿خَيْرٌ مِن ألْفِ شَهْرٍ﴾ ("better than a thousand months"): than a thousand months in which there is no Night of Decree.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿تَنَـزَّلُ المَلائِكَةُ والرُّوحُ فِيها بِإذْنِ رَبِّهِمْ مِن كُلِّ أمْرٍ﴾ ("the angels and the Spirit descend therein by the permission of their Lord with every matter"): the angels descend with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, decrees on the Night of Decree for the year, until the [next] Night of Decree comes. It was also read: ”مِن كُلِّ امْرِئٍ“ ("from every person"); this reading differs from the Muṣḥaf, except that it has been related from Ibn ʿAbbās.

zajjaj:5-5.t: And His saying: ﴿سَلامٌ هي حَتّى مَطْلَعِ الفَجْرِ﴾ ("peace it is until the rising of the dawn"): that is, there is no ill in it, and Satan is unable to do any evil in it. And ”اَلرُّوحُ“ is Gabriel, peace be upon him. It was read ”مَطْلَعِ الفَجْرِ“ and ”مَطْلِعِ الفَجْرِ“, with fatḥa and kasra on the lām. Whoever reads it with fatḥa, it is the maṣdar (verbal noun), meaning ”اَلطُّلُوعُ“ ("rising"): you say ”طَلَعَ الفَجْرَ طُلُوعًا ومَطْلَعًا“ ("the dawn rose, a rising"). And whoever says ”مَطْلِعِ“, it is a noun for the time of rising, and likewise for the place of rising: the noun is ”مَطْلِعٌ“ with kasra on the lām. [Translator's note: the source prints «طَلَعَ الفَجْرَ» with accusative «الفَجْرَ»; read «الفَجْرُ», as the agent.]
